questions.q: How long before clinical features can antibodies appear in SLE according to the opening comparison?
questions.exp: Antibodies can appear before clinical features: SLE 3 years; Sjogren syndrome 10–15 years. (Book p455)

questions.q: When ANA is positive, which technique is identified as useful for assessing pattern?
questions.exp: ANA methodology: ELISA is only for quantitative assessment; IIF/indirect IF on HEp-2 cells, with titre >1:80, is used to look for pattern. (Book p455)

questions.q: What ANA titre threshold is shown in the positive-ANA flowchart before proceeding to pattern review?
questions.exp: The flowchart shows IIF (HEp-2) and titre >1:80, then look for pattern. (Book p455)

questions.q: ANA shows dense fine speckling in mitotic-phase cells. What is the disease implication given in the table?
questions.exp: Dense fine speckled pattern in mitotic-phase cells has no probable antibody listed and rules out CTD. (Book p455)

questions.q: A fine-speckled ANA pattern is accompanied by anti-Ro/La. Which disease association should be selected?
questions.exp: Fine speckled pattern is linked to anti-Ro/La and Sjogren syndrome. (Book p455)

questions.q: A coarse-speckled ANA pattern with anti-Smith antibody is associated with which disease?
questions.exp: Coarse speckled patterns include anti-Smith → SLE, anti-U1 RNP → MCTD, and anti-RNA polymerase 3 → systemic sclerosis. (Book p455)

questions.q: Which antibody–disease association is correct for coarse-speckled ANA?
questions.exp: The coarse-speckled table maps anti-U1 RNP to MCTD. (Book p455)

questions.q: A nucleolar ANA pattern with PM/Scl-70 points to which overlap?
questions.exp: Nucleolar pattern with PM/Scl-70 is linked to polymyositis–scleroderma overlap. (Book p455)

questions.q: Which antibody is linked to cytoplasmic ANA pattern and antisynthetase syndrome?
questions.exp: Cytoplasmic pattern with anti-Jo-1 is linked to polymyositis/dermatomyositis (antisynthetase syndrome). (Book p455)

questions.q: Which homogeneous ANA pairing is correctly stated?
questions.exp: Homogeneous pattern: anti-dsDNA associates with SLE and antihistone with drug-induced SLE. (Book p455)

questions.q: A centromere ANA pattern is associated with which disease?
questions.exp: The final row maps centromere pattern to CREST syndrome (scleroderma). (Book p455)

questions.q: After a positive ANA and IIF pattern, what is the source’s next diagnostic step?
opts: Further evaluation to confirm antibodies with ANA or ENA profile
Immediate renal biopsy in every patient
questions.exp: Clinical suspicion → ANA positive → IIF pattern → further evaluation to confirm antibodies, using ANA profile or ENA profile. (Book p456)

questions.q: Which statement describes the ANA profile on the page?
opts: Immunoblot-based, costly multiple-antibody analysis, done once without repeat values
A cheap bedside test repeated daily
questions.exp: ANA profile: by immunoblot, costly/multiple antibody analysis, done once (no repeat values). ENA profile tests six antibodies. (Book p456)

questions.q: Which disease is stated to have ANA positivity in 100% of cases in the flowchart?
opts: Mixed connective-tissue disease, drug-induced lupus and type 1 autoimmune hepatitis
questions.exp: ANA positivity chart: 100% MCTD, DILE and type 1 autoimmune hepatitis; 85% Sjogren; 50% IgG4-related disease. In SLE it is positive in 97%. (Book p456)

questions.q: What caution is given about ANA in rheumatoid arthritis?
opts: ANA is not diagnostic despite RA being the most common multisystem CTD
questions.exp: The source says RA is the most common multisystem CTD but ANA is not diagnostic. (Book p456)

questions.q: A patient has DILE. Which antibody and IIF pattern combination fits the source?
opts: Antihistone antibody with homogeneous IIF pattern
questions.exp: DILE features: 100% ANA positive, homogeneous IIF pattern, antihistone antibody positive, and procainamide cause. (Book p456)

questions.q: Which drug is named as a cause of drug-induced lupus erythematosus?
questions.exp: The DILE block lists procainamide as a cause. (Book p456)

questions.q: What atypical antibody pattern is noted in elderly SLE?
opts: Anti-dsDNA positive with low complement always
questions.exp: Note: elderly SLE → anti-Ro positive and ANA negative. (Book p456)

questions.q: Which technique is listed for anti-dsDNA titre measurement?
questions.exp: Anti-dsDNA: ELISA for titre; Crithidia luciliae (flagella) is a qualitative IIF method marked obsolete. (Book p457)

questions.q: Which test organism/method is used qualitatively for anti-dsDNA in the source, though marked obsolete?
questions.exp: Crithidia luciliae (flagella) is specified as qualitative IIF, obsolete. (Book p457)

questions.q: Which comparison of anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith is correct on the page?
opts: Anti-dsDNA sensitivity 75% (preferred); anti-Smith 25% but more specific
Anti-Smith is 75% sensitive and anti-dsDNA 25% specific
questions.exp: Table: anti-dsDNA sensitivity 75% preferred; anti-Smith 25% more specific. (Book p457)

questions.q: Serial anti-dsDNA titres are rising. Which risks are specifically noted to rise?
questions.exp: The source states increased anti-dsDNA titres increase nephritis and vasculitis risk; no prognostic effect is listed for anti-Smith. (Book p457)

questions.q: What is the source’s general interpretation of anti-Ro/La in an asymptomatic person?
questions.exp: Anti-Ro/La is non-specific in CTD and has no significance in asymptomatic patients. (Book p457)

questions.q: In a patient with SLE, anti-Ro/La positivity indicates which associated condition?
questions.exp: Within SLE, anti-Ro/La indicates secondary Sjogren; it is also linked to pregnancy CHB, SCLE/HLA-DR3/photosensitive lesions, good prognosis and lupus myocarditis. (Book p457)

questions.q: What congenital-heart-block risk is given for pregnancy with anti-Ro/La positivity?
questions.exp: In pregnancy, anti-Ro/La is linked to 2–5% congenital heart block, increased in female child. (Book p457)

questions.q: A patient with SCLE, photosensitive lesions and HLA-DR3 positivity has anti-Ro/La. What is the source’s renal/vascular prognosis association of higher titres?
opts: Lower risk of nephritis and vasculitis
Higher risk of nephritis and vasculitis
questions.exp: Anti-Ro/La is associated with SCLE/HLA-DR3/photosensitivity and good prognosis: higher titres → reduced risk of nephritis/vasculitis; it is protective in skin/myocardium and linked to shrinking-lung syndrome. (Book p457)

questions.q: About what fraction of SLE patients have antiphospholipid-syndrome antibodies according to the page?
questions.exp: APS antibodies are positive in one-third of SLE patients. (Book p457)

questions.q: Warm-antibody autoimmune haemolytic anaemia in SLE is associated with which antibody?
questions.exp: The antibody list identifies anti-RBC antibody in warm-antibody autoimmune haemolytic anaemia. (Book p457)

questions.q: Anti-platelet antibody is listed in secondary ITP associated with which group?
opts: SLE, HIV, hepatitis C, H. pylori and RA
questions.exp: Secondary ITP list: SLE, HIV, hepatitis C, H. pylori and RA, with bleeding/anaemia. (Book p457)

questions.q: Which antibody is specific for psychosis/depression in CNS lupus on the source page?
questions.exp: Anti-ribosomal P is specific for psychosis/depression in CNS lupus; anti-glutamate/anti-neuronal antibody is most common in CNS lupus. (Book p457)

questions.q: What is the most common CNS manifestation of lupus according to the note?
questions.exp: The note names cognitive decline as the most common CNS manifestation in lupus. (Book p457)

questions.q: Which combination is listed as biomarkers of SLE disease activity?
opts: Anti-dsDNA titre, low C3/C4, and raised ESR with low CRP
Anti-Ro titre, high C3/C4, and high CRP
questions.exp: Biomarkers: anti-dsDNA titre, ↓C3/↓C4, and ↑ESR with ↓CRP. (Book p457)

units.title: 1. ANA Methodology, Titre & Pattern Interpretation
units.guide:
Antibody timing and ANA methodology come before the pattern table.
Cell-cycle staining, antigen specificity and CTD association are tested as clinical interpretations.
The chapter then moves from positive ANA to a targeted profile.

units.title: 2. ANA Profile, DILE & Clinical Approach
units.guide:
IIF-confirmed ANA leads to profile selection and test limitations.
Disease-specific positivity frequencies are separated from diagnostic specificity.
Drug-induced lupus retains its pattern, antibody and source-listed culprit.

units.title: 3. SLE Antibodies, Prognosis & Activity
units.guide:
Anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith are compared for sensitivity and prognostic value.
Anti-Ro/La is positioned in pregnancy, cutaneous lupus and systemic associations.
Less-common antibodies and source activity biomarkers close the diagnostic sequence.
